evidence: common/src/main/java/org/keycloak/common/crypto/CryptoIntegration.java:66 does builder.append(name + ", "). The claim is technically accurate: an intermediate String is created per iteration. But this runs once, in detectProvider (the provider is cached), over a list of 2-3 providers, only on the >1-provider debug path. Since JDK 9, javac compiles '+' to an invokedynamic StringConcatFactory call, so the cost is negligible. Chaining .append() is slightly more idiomatic, but the practical impact is nil. A cleaner fix that also resolves issue 2 is to stream-map the class names and use Collectors.joining(", ").

authz/client/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/util/crypto/AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java:114-115 call ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger/sBigInteger) and throw the results away. ASN1Encoder.java:42-49 shows create() returns a new instance with its own private ByteArrayOutputStream, and write() only writes to that stream. There is no shared state or other side effect. Lines 117-121 rebuild both encoders for writeDerSeq, so 114-115 are dead code (leftover debugging) and should be removed.

CryptoIntegration.java:64-68: the loop appends name + ", " for every ignored provider, including the last one, then logs builder.toString(). The debug message therefore always ends with a trailing ", ". This is cosmetic and only affects a debug log, but it is real and easy to fix with String.join, Collectors.joining, or StringJoiner. While doing that, pass the string as an argument (logger.debugf("Ignored crypto providers: %s", ...)) rather than as the format string, and avoid building it when debug is disabled.

AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java:130 throws IOException("Invalid sequence with size different to 2"). 'Different to' is standard British English (Oxford and Cambridge dictionaries list it alongside 'different from'), so it is not a grammatical error. 'Different from' is more common in US/technical English, but the message is clear either way. It is an exception string with no functional impact.
